items.title: Student-First AI Policy
items.authors: By Shaleen Title, Brendan Bouffard, and Joan Donovan, PhD
items.summary: The Student-First AI Policy gives local school districts a vetting process for any AI tool they consider putting in front of students. Before a product reaches students, it requires independent evidence that it improves learning, protects student privacy, and will not perpetuate discrimination or existing inequities.
items.imageAlt: Cover of the Student-First AI Policy

items.title: From Legal Reform to Market Formation
items.authors: By Damian Fagon and Shanel Lindsay
items.summary: Drawing on international expert convenings in Salem, Prague, and Rio de Janeiro, this report separates the regulatory capacity that can transfer between jurisdictions from the commercial market structures that don’t, and identifies design levers that reduce exclusion in emerging cannabis markets.
items.imageAlt: Cover of the From Legal Reform to Market Formation report

items.title: The Illusion of Competition
items.authors: By Damian Fagon and Hedy Yang
items.summary: Our new report on the Illinois market maps every active cannabis brand in Illinois to the parent company that controls it, and finds market concentration rising again. That outcome was produced by policy choices: a licensing framework that gave incumbents a multiyear head start, regulators too fragmented to intervene, and a tax structure that hits small producers hardest.
items.imageAlt: Cover of The Illusion of Competition report

items.title: Consumer Perspectives in States with Established Cannabis Markets
items.authors: By Faith English and Meredith McGee
items.summary: Drawing on 37 in-depth interviews with cannabis consumers across nine states where adult-use cannabis has been legal for at least five years, this study shows how consumers see the benefits and limits of legalization in their communities.
items.imageAlt: Cover of the consumer research study, “I Like Not Having to Go Behind the Dumpster at a Taco Bell”
